title: Host GPU capacity follow-up: tiered eviction and graceful-decline to curb queue amplification
creator: Marcus Li
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity surge on 2026-02-26 we observed a multi-minute GPU exhaustion window caused by a combination of sudden request amplification from large-batch inference jobs and aggressive admission policies that allowed queue buildup. The result: long tail latency, cascading queue growth across pools, and throttling spikes that impacted premium customers. Root causes identified: 1) admission gating did not enforce progressive degradation for low-priority traffic; 2) eviction policy was single-tier LRU which caused synchronized eviction storms; 3) no priming path for standby capacity, so scale-up laged under sudden parallelism spikes. This ticket tracks follow-up work to implement a tiered-eviction model (multi-level fairness + soft eviction), a graceful-decline admission path (progressive request degradation rather than hard rejects), and adaptive-priming to reduce cold-scale latency. Goals: reduce queue amplification amplification factor by >= 4x under burst loads, restore P99 latency SLO within 2x baseline during extreme bursts, and eliminate customer-facing 5xxs caused by orchestration timeouts.
acceptance_criteria: Tiered eviction algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests and integration tests
Graceful-decline admission mode enabled behind a feature flag; low-priority traffic receives best-effort degraded responses instead of queueing indefinitely
Adaptive-priming reduces median scale-up time by at least 30% in synthetic surge tests
End-to-end runbooks updated and can be executed without manual DB changes

Performance verification: synthetic workload (10k concurrent small requests + 500 concurrent large-batch requests) shows queue amplification factor <= 1.5x and P99 token-latency within target for release runtime-1.22
tasks: Design tiered-eviction data model (credits, tiers, soft-priority drop) — design doc in Confluence
Engineer runtime admission API to support graceful-decline responses and token-level dropping
Implement adaptive-priming heuristics in autoscaler to pre-warm standby nodes for bursty customers
Add end-to-end integration tests in runtime CI for surge scenarios
Add observability: per-pool amplification metric, per-tier evictions, graceful-decline rate
Create canary rollout plan and rollback criteria; coordinate with SRE and CS for high-impact customers
Update runbooks and incident pages with new mitigation steps
comments: 2026-03-01 Marcus Li: Created ticket based on postmortem (see confluence summary) — initial scope drafted. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GPU+Capacity+Exhaustion+Postmortem

2026-03-02 Ava Patel: Ran local spike tests to reproduce queue amplification. Observed synchronized eviction when pool filled; current LRU eviction window ~120s causes backpressure waves. Attached profiling notes: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-capacity/queue-metrics?orgId=1

2026-03-03 Elena Gomez (SRE): Recommendation to prefer soft-decline for non-SLA traffic as temporary mitigation. Suggested feature-flag rollout and an emergency kill-switch in allocator controller. Linked runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-exhaustion

2026-03-04 Marcus Li: Design decision meeting notes — opted for a 3-tier eviction model (SLA, work-conserving, best-effort). Each request consumes tier credits; eviction prefers draining best-effort first. Decision doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654

2026-03-05 Ava Patel: PoC implemented for graceful-decline: runtime returns streaming partial tokens + 'degraded_output' header for requests subjected to decline. PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 — awaiting review from @elena and @rahul

2026-03-06 Rahul Mehta (Principal Infra): Reviewed PoC; requested stronger invariants around cache/KV retention during soft declines to avoid correctness regressions. Also flagged potential interaction with function-calling timeouts. Action: add regression tests for function-calling flows.

2026-03-07 Ava Patel: Implemented adaptive-priming heuristic using recent customer burst history and pre-allocated standby instances with conservative spill ratios. Benchmarks: scale-up median reduced from 18s to 11s on our synthetic workload. Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-capacity/priming-benchmarks

2026-03-09 Marcus Li: Security/Compliance review: graceful-decline does not persist customer PII; responses are generated from model as usual. Verified KMS/HSM unaffected. Recorded note for audit: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Graceful+Decline+Review

2026-03-10 SRE Ops (Elena Gomez): Runbook updated with new mitigation steps: toggle 'graceful-decline' flag, adjust tier thresholds, and force-evict best-effort. Playbook added to incident runbooks. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/78

2026-03-11 Ava Patel: Integration tests added to CI with surge scenario. Observability added: 'queue_amplification_factor' and 'evictions_by_tier' metrics. Tests green locally; running in staging CI. GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1267

2026-03-12 Marcus Li: Prepared canary rollout plan — 10% traffic to new algorithm in us-west-2 first 2 hours, monitor P99 and 5xx rate. Rollback if 5xx > 0.1% or P99 regresses > 1.5x baseline. Canary doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/deployments/canary-plans#tiered-eviction

2026-03-13 PM Feedback (Jen Park): Prioritize customers with active incidents for immediate small-scale canary to reduce exposure. Action: coordinate CS to opt those customers into canary. Added as follow-up task.
notes: Trade-offs: soft-decline improves availability but may degrade perceived model output quality. We will gate by labels (best-effort only) and provide explicit headers so SDKs can surface degraded mode to apps.
Edge-case: Function-calling flows may expect structured outputs. We'll skip graceful-decline for function-calls until regression tests confirm safety.
Longer-term: Evaluate integrating admission logic with cost-aware routing and dedicated pools to reduce impact on SLAs. Consider making tier thresholds customer-configurable for Dedicated customers.
